attitude_axis: crime; policing; federal grants; wiretaps; public order
benchmark_question: Should federal law expand crime-control grants while authorizing and regulating wiretapping for law enforcement?
predicted_time_profile: Low in Warren Court rights-expansion frame; rises with 1960s public-order and crime politics
notes: CAP/Congress.gov source-frame addition; links crime politics and surveillance.

adoption_object: Require standardized disclosure of consumer-credit costs and terms
attitude_axis: consumer protection; credit markets; disclosure; financial regulation
benchmark_question: Should federal law require lenders to disclose standardized credit costs and terms to consumers?
predicted_time_profile: Low before mass consumer credit; rises with 1960s consumer-protection politics; baseline for later credit/privacy law
notes: CAP/Congress Project consumer-credit omission; pairs with FCRA, ECOA, CRA.

adoption_object: Regulate consumer-reporting agencies and create accuracy, access, and privacy protections for credit files
attitude_axis: privacy; credit; data accuracy; consumer protection
benchmark_question: Should federal law give consumers rights over credit-reporting files and regulate consumer-reporting agencies?
predicted_time_profile: Low before mass computerized credit reporting; rises with 1960s-1970s consumer/privacy politics
notes: Promoted from round-1 deferred; important data/privacy precursor.

adoption_object: Create the Consumer Product Safety Commission and federal consumer-product safety authority
attitude_axis: consumer protection; safety; expert regulation; product markets
benchmark_question: Should federal law create an independent agency to protect consumers from unsafe products?
predicted_time_profile: Low before 1960s consumer movement; high by early 1970s regulatory expansion; contested in deregulation era
notes: Promoted from round-1 deferred after consumer-regulation source-frame check.

adoption_object: Create the Strategic Petroleum Reserve and federal energy-conservation tools after the oil shock
attitude_axis: energy security; oil crisis; conservation; federal planning
benchmark_question: Should federal law create strategic petroleum reserves and energy-conservation authority after an oil shock?
predicted_time_profile: Low before 1970s energy crisis; high after embargo and stagflation; later reframed around efficiency and climate
notes: Promoted from round-1 deferred; core energy-crisis policy row.

adoption_object: Uphold federal highway-fund conditions tied to state drinking-age policy
attitude_axis: federalism; spending power; alcohol; conditional grants
benchmark_question: Should Congress be able to condition a small share of federal highway funds on states raising the drinking age?
predicted_time_profile: Low before grant-in-aid state capacity; high in late twentieth-century conditional-spending doctrine; limited by NFIB coercion concerns
notes: Promoted from round-1 deferred; spending-power doctrine bridge to NFIB.

adoption_object: Invalidate Communications Decency Act restrictions on indecent internet speech
attitude_axis: internet; speech; child protection; censorship; new media
benchmark_question: Should broad federal restrictions on indecent online speech survive First Amendment review?
predicted_time_profile: Not meaningful before mass internet; plausible during early internet moral panic; invalidation high in speech-protective doctrine
notes: Promoted from round-1 deferred; technology/speech expansion.

policy_or_case: Kelo v. City of New London
adoption_object: Uphold use of eminent domain for economic-development transfer to private redevelopment
attitude_axis: property rights; economic development; local redevelopment; public use
benchmark_question: Should government be able to use eminent domain for an economic-development plan involving transfer to private redevelopers?
predicted_time_profile: More plausible under deferential midcentury redevelopment doctrine; politically toxic after property-rights backlash
notes: Promoted from round-1 deferred; property/development backlash benchmark.

adoption_object: Create a federally owned corporation to build dams, generate public power, control floods, and promote regional economic development in the Tennessee Valley.
attitude_axis: public ownership, regional planning, federal development state, electric power, New Deal state capacity
benchmark_question: Would the federal government create a public corporation to transform a multi-state region through dams, electricity, flood control, and planning?
predicted_time_profile: Low before the Depression, sharply higher by 1933, later normalized as part of New Deal state-capacity memory.
notes: Round-3 NARA milestone omission; distinct from relief programs because it tests public ownership and regional planning.

adoption_object: Authorize industry codes, public works spending, and collective-bargaining protections as an emergency economic recovery program.
attitude_axis: planning, industrial codes, labor rights, emergency state capacity, constitutional limits
benchmark_question: Would Congress adopt a sweeping industrial-recovery statute that lets the federal government coordinate industry codes and labor standards?
predicted_time_profile: Rises sharply in the Depression emergency, then falls doctrinally after Schechter while remaining historically central.
notes: Separate adoption row from the existing Schechter invalidation row.

adoption_object: Authorize military exclusion zones that enabled the forced removal and incarceration of Japanese Americans during World War II.
attitude_axis: race, national security, civil liberties, wartime executive power, exclusion
benchmark_question: Would the President authorize mass exclusion and incarceration of a racialized minority during wartime on national-security grounds?
predicted_time_profile: Low in ordinary periods, sharply higher after Pearl Harbor, then morally and legally delegitimized after the war.
notes: Adds the policy-adoption counterpart to the existing Korematsu judicial-validation row.

adoption_object: Commit the United States to support governments resisting communist pressure, beginning with aid to Greece and Turkey.
attitude_axis: anti-communism, internationalism, containment, foreign aid, Cold War statecraft
benchmark_question: Would the United States make anti-communist containment a central justification for foreign aid and security commitments?
predicted_time_profile: Low in interwar isolationist priors, higher after World War II, central by the early Cold War.
notes: NARA milestone source; complements Marshall Plan, NATO-era security state, and internal-security rows.

adoption_object: Use federal authority and troops to enforce school desegregation in Little Rock, Arkansas.
attitude_axis: civil-rights enforcement, federal troops, school desegregation, state resistance
benchmark_question: Would the President use federal executive power, including troops, to enforce court-ordered school desegregation against state resistance?
predicted_time_profile: Very low before Brown, higher after Brown and Little Rock, then part of the civil-rights enforcement repertoire.
notes: NARA milestone; adds executive-enforcement counterpart to Brown and Cooper.

adoption_object: Ratify a treaty banning nuclear weapons tests in the atmosphere, outer space, and underwater.
attitude_axis: nuclear risk, arms control, Cold War diplomacy, environmental fallout, national security
benchmark_question: Would the United States accept a binding nuclear arms-control treaty limiting atmospheric, underwater, and outer-space tests?
predicted_time_profile: Low in early Cold War maximalist testing politics, higher after fallout fears and the Cuban Missile Crisis.
notes: NARA milestone; adds a treaty/arms-control policy object absent from v3.

adoption_object: Authorize the President to use military force in Southeast Asia without a formal declaration of war.
attitude_axis: war powers, anti-communism, executive discretion, Vietnam, Cold War national security
benchmark_question: Would Congress give the President broad authority to use military force in Southeast Asia without declaring war?
predicted_time_profile: Rises with Cold War containment and Vietnam escalation, then becomes a backlash object for the War Powers Resolution.
notes: NARA milestone; essential counterpart to the existing War Powers Resolution row.

adoption_object: Prohibit employment discrimination against older workers.
attitude_axis: age, employment discrimination, civil rights, labor markets, protected classes
benchmark_question: Would Congress treat age discrimination in employment as a federal civil-rights problem?
predicted_time_profile: Low before the civil-rights employment framework, higher after Title VII and Great Society labor-rights expansion.
notes: OLRC popular-name source-frame omission; adds age to the anti-discrimination coverage set.

adoption_object: Require financial institutions to keep records and report certain transactions to help detect money laundering and financial crimes.
attitude_axis: financial privacy, surveillance, crime control, banking regulation, anti-money-laundering state capacity
benchmark_question: Would Congress require banks to report and preserve transaction information for federal law-enforcement and financial-surveillance purposes?
predicted_time_profile: Low before modern organized-crime and drug-policy concerns, higher by 1970, then expanded after terrorism and AML concerns.
notes: OLRC popular-name omission; complements FISA, Privacy Act, FCRA, PATRIOT Act, and financial regulation rows.

adoption_object: Settle Alaska Native land claims through land transfers, monetary compensation, and Native corporations.
attitude_axis: Native sovereignty, land claims, corporate settlement, resource development, self-determination
benchmark_question: Would Congress settle Native land claims through a large land-and-money settlement organized around Native corporations?
predicted_time_profile: Low under allotment/termination priors, higher around Alaska statehood, oil development, and the self-determination turn.
notes: OLRC and agency-source omission; fills a major Native-policy land-settlement gap.

adoption_object: Declare federal policy to protect and preserve American Indian, Alaska Native, and Native Hawaiian religious practices.
attitude_axis: Native religious freedom, cultural rights, sacred sites, federal land management
benchmark_question: Would Congress formally recognize protection of Native religious practices as a federal policy objective?
predicted_time_profile: Low under assimilation and termination-era priors, higher during the 1970s self-determination and rights turn.
notes: OLRC popular-name omission; useful even though the statute was more declaratory than enforcement-heavy.

adoption_object: Renew and amend the Voting Rights Act, including a results-based test for vote dilution under Section 2.
attitude_axis: racial vote dilution, federal voting-rights enforcement, results tests, civil-rights backlash
benchmark_question: Would Congress renew the Voting Rights Act and make vote-dilution liability turn on discriminatory results rather than intent alone?
predicted_time_profile: Low before the civil-rights era, high after 1965, contested but plausible amid 1980s rights retrenchment.
notes: OLRC popular-name omission; adds an important post-1965 voting-rights evolution.

adoption_object: Expand legal immigration, revise employment-based immigration, and create the diversity visa program.
attitude_axis: legal immigration, high-skill immigration, diversity visas, national origins reform aftermath
benchmark_question: Would Congress expand legal immigration and create new employment-based and diversity-visa channels?
predicted_time_profile: Low before Hart-Celler, higher after immigration liberalization, then contested amid 1990s immigration politics.
notes: OLRC popular-name omission; fills gap between IRCA and later immigration enforcement/restriction politics.

adoption_object: Require government to satisfy strict scrutiny when substantially burdening religious exercise.
attitude_axis: religious liberty, civil-rights coalitions, judicial backlash, statutory constitutionalism
benchmark_question: Would Congress restore a strict-scrutiny rule for burdens on religious exercise after the Supreme Court narrowed Free Exercise doctrine?
predicted_time_profile: Low before the Warren/Burger-era rights framework, high after Smith, then increasingly polarized in later religion/health conflicts.
notes: OLRC popular-name omission; important statutory bridge to Hobby Lobby and later religion cases.

policy_or_case: Antiterrorism and Effective Death Penalty Act
adoption_object: Restrict habeas corpus review, expand terrorism-related tools, and accelerate death-penalty procedures.
attitude_axis: terrorism, death penalty, habeas corpus, crime control, federal courts
benchmark_question: Would Congress respond to terrorism and crime concerns by restricting habeas review and accelerating capital-punishment procedures?
predicted_time_profile: Low in the Warren Court criminal-procedure period, higher by the 1990s crime/terrorism politics, contested after civil-liberties backlash.
notes: OLRC popular-name omission; fills a major criminal-justice/federal-courts restriction row.

policy_or_case: Illegal Immigration Reform and Immigrant Responsibility Act
adoption_object: Expand immigration enforcement, removal rules, inadmissibility bars, and penalties for unauthorized immigration.
attitude_axis: immigration restriction, border enforcement, deportation, criminalization, welfare-era retrenchment
benchmark_question: Would Congress sharply expand immigration enforcement and removal rules as part of a broader restrictionist turn?
predicted_time_profile: Low before late-20th-century immigration backlash, higher after IRCA and 1990s restrictionist politics.
notes: OLRC popular-name omission; complements Hart-Celler, Refugee Act, IRCA, and PRWORA.

policy_or_case: Authorization for Use of Military Force of 2001
adoption_object: Authorize the President to use force against those responsible for the September 11 attacks and associated harboring entities.
attitude_axis: terrorism, war powers, executive discretion, national security, civil liberties
benchmark_question: Would Congress give the President broad open-ended authority to use military force against terrorism-linked actors after a major attack?
predicted_time_profile: Low before 9/11, extremely high immediately after 9/11, then increasingly contested as the war on terror persisted.
notes: GovInfo/OLRC omission; essential counterpart to PATRIOT Act and war-powers rows.

policy_or_case: Authorization for Use of Military Force Against Iraq Resolution of 2002
adoption_object: Authorize the President to use military force against Iraq.
attitude_axis: Iraq War, terrorism, weapons of mass destruction, executive war powers, national security
benchmark_question: Would Congress authorize military force against Iraq under post-9/11 national-security and weapons-of-mass-destruction claims?
predicted_time_profile: Low before 9/11, high during 2002 security politics, then strongly contested after the Iraq War backlash.
notes: GovInfo/OLRC omission; distinct from the 2001 AUMF and useful for backlash time profiles.

adoption_object: Reset the limitations period for pay-discrimination claims with each discriminatory paycheck.
attitude_axis: gender pay equity, employment discrimination, courts versus Congress, civil-rights enforcement
benchmark_question: Would Congress override a Supreme Court limitations ruling to make pay-discrimination claims easier to bring?
predicted_time_profile: Low before Title VII and modern gender equality politics, higher after feminist labor-rights mobilization and Ledbetter.
notes: OLRC popular-name omission; adds a congressional override/civil-rights-enforcement row.

policy_or_case: Matthew Shepard and James Byrd Jr. Hate Crimes Prevention Act
adoption_object: Expand federal hate-crimes law to cover crimes motivated by gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, or disability.
attitude_axis: hate crimes, LGBTQ rights, race, gender identity, disability, federal criminal enforcement
benchmark_question: Would Congress expand federal hate-crime law to protect LGBTQ people, people with disabilities, and other targeted groups?
predicted_time_profile: Low before modern hate-crime and LGBTQ-rights politics, higher by the 2000s.
notes: OLRC/GovInfo omission; bridges civil-rights criminal enforcement and LGBTQ-rights expansion.

policy_or_case: Don't Ask, Don't Tell Repeal Act
adoption_object: Repeal the statutory basis for excluding openly gay, lesbian, and bisexual people from military service.
attitude_axis: LGBTQ rights, military service, national security culture, sexuality
benchmark_question: Would Congress repeal the ban on openly gay, lesbian, and bisexual people serving in the military?
predicted_time_profile: Very low before gay-rights mobilization, still low around 1993 compromise politics, high by 2010.
notes: OLRC popular-name omission; complements Bowers, Lawrence, DOMA, Windsor, Obergefell, and Bostock.

adoption_object: Reduce some federal sentences, expand earned-time credits, and reform federal prison programming.
attitude_axis: mass incarceration, sentencing reform, bipartisan criminal-justice reform, drug sentencing
benchmark_question: Would Congress adopt a bipartisan federal sentencing and prison reform after decades of punitive criminal-justice politics?
predicted_time_profile: Low during the 1980s-1990s punitive turn, higher after mass-incarceration critique became mainstream.
notes: GovInfo/OLRC omission; adds criminal-justice retrenchment/reform after the 1994 crime bill.

adoption_object: Enact large-scale COVID-era fiscal relief, including stimulus payments, expanded child tax credit, unemployment support, and state and local aid.
attitude_axis: pandemic relief, fiscal state capacity, child poverty, stimulus, federal aid
benchmark_question: Would Congress enact a large emergency relief package with direct payments, expanded family benefits, and state/local aid in response to a pandemic?
predicted_time_profile: Low before modern crisis-fiscal policy, higher after the Great Recession and very high during COVID.
notes: GovInfo public-law scan omission; complements CARES but tests a different welfare/fiscal profile.

adoption_object: Adopt a large bipartisan infrastructure package for transportation, broadband, water, energy, and resilience projects.
attitude_axis: infrastructure, industrial policy, federal investment, bipartisan public works, broadband
benchmark_question: Would Congress adopt a large bipartisan federal infrastructure package spanning transportation, broadband, water, and energy systems?
predicted_time_profile: Plausible in New Deal/highway-era state-capacity priors, lower during austerity/deregulation periods, higher again in 2020s industrial-policy politics.
notes: GovInfo public-law scan omission; modern public-investment anchor after ARRA and CHIPS/IRA.

adoption_object: Make Juneteenth a federal legal public holiday.
attitude_axis: racial memory, emancipation, federal commemoration, civil-rights recognition
benchmark_question: Would Congress make Juneteenth a federal holiday commemorating emancipation?
predicted_time_profile: Low before modern civil-rights memory politics, higher after Black freedom history became part of federal commemorative practice.
notes: GovInfo public-law scan omission; more symbolic than regulatory but useful for attitudes toward federal racial-memory recognition.

adoption_object: Adopt federal gun-safety, mental-health, school-safety, and background-check changes after mass shootings.
attitude_axis: guns, mass shootings, mental health, background checks, bipartisan safety regulation
benchmark_question: Would Congress enact a bipartisan federal gun-safety package after mass shootings despite polarized gun politics?
predicted_time_profile: Low before late-20th-century gun-control politics, higher after recurring mass-shooting politics but still sharply contested.
notes: OLRC/GovInfo omission; important post-Heller/Bruen congressional gun-policy event.

adoption_object: Repeal DOMA and require federal and interstate recognition of valid same-sex and interracial marriages.
attitude_axis: same-sex marriage, interracial marriage, federal recognition, LGBTQ rights, post-Dobbs legal uncertainty
benchmark_question: Would Congress repeal DOMA and require recognition of valid same-sex marriages across federal and state lines?
predicted_time_profile: Very low before gay-rights normalization, low around DOMA, high after Obergefell and Dobbs-driven statutory-protection politics.
notes: OLRC/GovInfo omission; essential statutory counterpart to DOMA, Windsor, Obergefell, and Dobbs.

adoption_object: Clarify and revise procedures for counting electoral votes and limit avenues for overturning presidential election results.
attitude_axis: democratic procedure, presidential elections, peaceful transfer of power, election subversion, institutional reform
benchmark_question: Would Congress reform the Electoral Count Act to reduce ambiguity and constrain attempts to overturn presidential election results?
predicted_time_profile: Low before 2020 election-subversion crisis, sharply higher after January 6 and bipartisan institutional alarm.
notes: OLRC/GovInfo omission; major democracy-procedure row after Bush v. Gore and Rucho.
